deepdive.sec: Financial Services — Microfinance / Diversified rural NBFC (MFI + Housing Finance + MSME/Green Finance + emerging Tech & AIF units)

bull_bear.body: Funding: raised ₹10,826cr in FY26 across 75 active lenders; maintains ₹2,092cr balance-sheet liquidity + ₹2,235cr undrawn sanctions, ALM positive across all buckets. Well capitalized — standalone CRAR 25.4%. SGAL's SEBI-licensed AIF (₹200cr target corpus, SBI co-investment MOU) represents a new fee-income/AUM-based capital-allocation vector outside the core balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Forex/treasury P&L lines (derecognition gain, fair-value gain) are large and can swing quarter to quarter purely on timing/dollar movement even though fully hedged over the cycle (FY25 full-year net impact was -₹25cr) — watch for distortion in any single quarter's reported PAT.
- Sector-wide dependence on continued "healing" — PAR 1-180 days at 4.7% as of Jan-2026 (down from peak 6-7 months earlier); a reversal in disbursement growth or borrower overleveraging could reintroduce stress.
- Geopolitical/inflation risk flagged by an analyst; management's view is inflation upticks tend to increase credit demand over time rather than suppress it, but near-term income-level pressure was acknowledged.
- No explicit ROA guidance given — makes FY27 profitability trajectory harder to pin down precisely; investors should model off AUM growth + credit-cost guidance rather than a stated ROA target.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, data-dense tone from Dr. H.P. Singh, leaning on the 35-year track record and explicit avoidance of one-off explanations for strong results (repeatedly and directly denied any one-off when pressed by an analyst). CFO/Group Controller (Jugal Kataria) and CSO (Aditi Singh) handled granular numeric follow-ups (credit-cost splits, forex-line explanations) directly and transparently, including admitting inability to give a firm ROA guidance rather than over-promising.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Standalone net worth being *higher* than consolidated net worth (₹3,129cr vs ₹2,868cr) is a legacy revaluation-gain accounting quirk from a subsidiary investment revaluation 5-6 years ago — not a red flag, but worth knowing before comparing standalone vs consol leverage ratios.
- Management is deliberately not chasing the industry shift toward individual (non-JLG) loans — running only small pilots — while several peers are pivoting harder toward individual lending; this is a differentiated strategic stance worth tracking versus peer commentary.
- The ₹25,000cr → ₹32,000cr FY30 AUM target upgrade came purely from subsidiary outperformance (SFL +92.5% YoY, Housing 36% 3yr CAGR) — a tangible, quantified reason for raising the long-term target rather than a vague aspirational bump.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Promoters will infuse Rs 100 Crores of equity share capital at roughly a 17% premium to the SEBI minimum issue price, presented as evidence of promoter commitment.
- Long history of capital access with 16 successful fund raises since inception and promoter participation in 14 of them; promoter holding stands at 36.2% with Florintree Ventures LLP at 11.1%.
- Conservative provisioning stance: on-book provisions of Rs 252 Crores (2.5% of the on-book portfolio) versus an RBI requirement of Rs 152 Crores, a Rs 36 Crores management overlay held as a buffer, Stage 3 coverage of 85% and overall provision coverage of 115%.
- Funding mix is diversified across term loans and PTC (53.1%), direct assignment (21.5%), NCDs (13.5%) and ECB (11.8%), sourced 70.4% from banks with the top 10 lenders at 52% of borrowings.
- Balance sheet run conservatively with standalone leverage of 3.15x, standalone CRAR of 26.7% and undrawn sanctions of ~Rs 2,600 Crores; the deck makes no mention of dividends.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Satin Housing Finance Ltd:** AUM ₹1,267cr, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA 3%; CRAR 53.8%; ICRA rating A- (stable). Customer mix: self-employed professionals + salaried; management sees the mix shifting further toward self-employed over the next 3–5 years. Average yield ~15.5–16%.
- **Satin Finserv Ltd:** AUM ₹1,054cr, +92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; operates across 14 states / 121 branches. Secured lending (receivables, hypothecation of equipment, movable property; LTV ~40–45%) with zero customer overlap with MFI book (a customer must give up their MFI loan to take a subsidiary loan). Green finance book: ₹255cr disbursed across 34 loans (solar, EVs, renewable energy micro-enterprises); yield close to MFI levels (~25%).
- **Satin Technologies Ltd (STL):** Newly incorporated; builds enterprise tech (HRMS, loan management systems, core banking, cybersecurity) with agentic AI as a horizontal capability; acquired first 2 clients within 2 months of incorporation. Acquired a strategic stake in QTrino (IIT-Patna-incubated post-quantum cryptography deep-tech firm) in Jan-2026; has representative offices in Toronto and Dubai.
- **Satin Growth Alternatives Ltd (SGAL):** Received SEBI license for a ₹200cr Category II AIF — a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs, led by an all-women team. Signed an MOU with State Bank of India for co-investment; progressing toward first close with "strong soft commitments."
- **Standalone net worth (₹3,129cr) exceeds consolidated net worth (₹2,868cr)** because of a historical (5–6 years ago, post-demonetization) revaluation gain booked on the parent's investment in subsidiaries at the standalone level, which is eliminated on consolidation.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **35-year institutional track record** navigating demonetization, COVID and the current MFI stress cycle — management cites this repeatedly as the reason for superior underwriting discipline and CXO team stability (avg. tenure >10 years).
- **Underwriting discipline evidenced in numbers:** sourcing-to-disbursement ratio of just 39% (reflects selectivity); borrower leverage policy caps at 3 MFI lenders / ₹2 lakh exposure; NATCAT insurance covering ₹5,800cr of disbursements since Sep-2025 to derisk against natural-catastrophe defaults.
- **Geographic risk management:** even in historically risky states, asset quality is now strong — Assam (once a risk state) PAR90 at just 0.7% with 100% collection efficiency; UP (largest state, 23% of book) PAR90 at 3%; Punjab 1.5%. All top states show 99.9–100% X-bucket collection efficiency.
- **Scale/reach barrier:** presence in 64% of India's pin codes, 2,015 branches, 577 districts, 34 lakh customers — a distribution network not easily replicated.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:
> Challenges specifically discussed: (a) sector-wide MFI stress cycle (FY25) now healing with SRO/MFIN2.0 guardrails (lender cap, ₹2 lakh borrower exposure ceiling) reshaping the industry; (b) credit guarantee scheme aiding sector recovery; (c) geopolitical/inflation risk to near-term credit growth.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "By early 2026, the sector had passed its stress peak… microfinance originations grew 25.8% QoQ" — sector-wide MFI recovery post SRO guardrails | CREDITACC · 541770 · Financial Services (Microfinance) ⭐; SATIN itself (this call) ✅ | Weaker/overleveraged MFIs that failed guardrail compliance (unlisted/regional NBFC-MFIs, not specifically named on this call) | Well-capitalized, guardrail-compliant MFIs with strong collection efficiency and provisioning are best placed to capture the sector-wide recovery in disbursements and ticket sizes; ⭐ = sector-knowledge inference from StockMetadata (Microfinance Institutions industry), not stated on this call |
| "SRO guardrails, the free lender cap and the ₹2 lakh borrower exposure ceiling have meaningfully reshaped the lending landscape" | FUSION · 543652 · Financial Services (Microfinance) ⭐; SPANDANA · 542759 · Financial Services (Microfinance) ⭐ | Smaller/undercapitalized MFIs unable to absorb compliance costs of tighter underwriting (not named) | Larger listed MFIs with the balance-sheet strength to absorb guardrail-driven underwriting tightening (as SATIN itself demonstrates with GNPA 3.1%, PAR90 <1% in stress states) are relative beneficiaries; ⭐ = sector-knowledge, not company-specific commentary |

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Frames itself as the only MFI with multiple growth engines - an ecosystem of microfinance/MSME lending, housing finance, equipment and green financing, supply chain finance, tech solutions and an AIF - versus mono-line NBFC-MFI peers.
- Claims a 35-year track record across demonetisation, Covid and the recent MFI industry stress, with a 17% AUM CAGR over a decade and 20 consecutive profitable quarters.
- Counter-cyclical share gain: Satin's AUM grew 14% in FY26 while the industry contracted 13% (industry AUM fell to Rs 3,31,000 Crores after 8 straight quarters of decline), and active borrowers were stable versus a 23% industry decline.
- Benchmarks ahead of peer averages on FY26 NIM (13.6% vs 12.3%), 3-year AUM CAGR (19% vs 7.7%), GNPA (3.1% vs 3.4%), credit cost (3.8% vs 6.4%), ROA (2.5% vs 1.8%) and ROE (10.1% vs 7.4%).
- Deep customer franchise with ~34 lakh borrowers and 37%+ of borrowers having vintage greater than 3 years.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Satin Technologies acquired a strategic stake in QTrino Labs, a deep-tech quantum-safe cybersecurity company, in Jan'26 and held 68% as of 30 June 2026; FIPS certification is in progress and Big 4 channel partnerships are advancing.
- [Regulation] MFIN Guardrails 2.0 has reshaped the industry - 95% of industry exposure is now to borrowers with 3 or fewer active lenders - and NBFC-MFIs gained ~480 bps of market share as banks' share fell ~600 bps, creating a favourable mix for Satin.
- [Funding innovation] Secured a Rs 2,000 Crores direct assignment sanction limit from a PSU through what the deck describes as its first ever digital-direct assignment.
- [Credit rating] Standalone rated ICRA A (Stable) long term and A1 short term, with both SHFL and SFL at ICRA A- (Stable).
- [Group structure] Four wholly owned subsidiaries - Satin Housing Finance, Satin Finserv, Satin Technologies and Satin Growth Alternatives - form the diversification vehicle, with SHFL net worth Rs 381 Crores and SFL net worth Rs 344 Crores.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Consol NIM improved from 12.42% (FY25) to 13.23% (FY26) despite the non-MFI mix rising — management attributes this to subsidiaries earning higher-than-typical yields for their asset classes (housing ~15.5–16% vs standard HFC rates; Satin Finserv near-MFI yields ~25%) because they serve the same underserved rural constituency. Cost of borrowing declined 43bps to 10.82% (marginal), driven partly by ~50bps reduction efforts; management expects funding costs to stay stable-to-lower as repo rates ease. Reported average incremental yield on core microfinance ~25–26%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol PAT +79% YoY for FY26 (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) on lower credit cost (3.8% vs 4.6% FY25); no one-offs per management despite large forex/treasury swing lines; non-MFI AUM at 17% (target 30% by 2030); FY30 consol AUM target raised ₹25,000cr → ₹32,000cr. FY27 guidance: standalone AUM +15-20%, consol +25-30%, credit cost 3-3.5%.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: credit cost trending toward 3-3.5% target; standalone AUM growth pace vs 15-20% guide; SFL/Housing AUM run-rate vs FY26 (~90%/38% growth); STL/SGAL traction (client wins, AIF first close); forex/treasury line volatility in the P&L; X-bucket collection efficiency holding at ~99.9%._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue/AUM growth (FY27):** Standalone (JLG-only) AUM growth guided at 15–20% YoY, implying ~₹14,800–15,100cr; consolidated growth guided higher at ~25–30% (blending standalone 15–20% with SFL ~90% YoY and Housing ~38% YoY growth in FY26).
- **Margin:** Credit cost target 3–3.5% for FY27 (vs 3.8% actual FY26) — "meaningful improvement." NIM guided to stay stable at 13.5–14% (consol ~12–13%) even as non-MFI mix rises, because subsidiaries operate in the same high-yield rural markets (housing finance yield ~15.5–16%, Satin Finserv yield close to MFI levels ~25%).
- **ROA/ROE:** No explicit numeric guidance given; management declined to commit but indicated it "will be positive from where we are right now" (FY26 consol ROA 2.6%) when asked if >3% ROA is achievable in FY27 — treat as a soft aspiration, not firm guidance.
- **Order book / long-term AUM target:** Consolidated AUM target for 2030 raised from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr, with non-MFI AUM target of 30% by 2030 (from 17% now).
- **Capex/expansion:** 392 new branches added in FY26 (total 2,015 branches / 577 districts); no major capex/commissioning items flagged (asset-light lending model).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not applicable in the traditional sense (lending business); pipeline visible via disbursement growth (standalone disbursements ₹11,202cr FY26) and branch expansion (392 new branches added FY26, presence across 1 lakh+ villages, 550+ districts, 64% of India's pin codes).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Diversification into non-MFI rural financial services (housing, secured MSME/green finance, enterprise tech, AIF/asset management) is the core optionality thesis — management explicitly frames subsidiaries as "two kickers" to ROA: Satin Technologies (capital-light, high-leverage-of-knowledge business) and Satin Growth Alternatives (fee/AUM-based, capital-light asset management). Individual-loan JLG pilots are underway but management is clear JLG will remain the mainstay (hybrid, not a shift).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 was a recovery year — consolidated PAT up 79% YoY (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) as credit cost normalized (FY26 3.8% vs 4.6% in FY25) and the sector passed its stress peak; management explicitly denies any one-off behind the Q4 PAT jump, attributing it to lower credit cost + growth. The diversification thesis is gaining traction — non-MFI AUM is 17% of consolidated book (target 30% by 2030) with Satin Housing and Satin Finserv each crossing ₹1,000cr AUM, prompting management to raise the FY30 consolidated AUM target from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr.

open.item: Entry into Kerala, a new state for the portfolio, with staff already hired and operations expected to be up and running in the next couple of months, alongside deeper penetration of existing geographies.
Management confirmed credit cost is expected to decrease in Q4FY26 from the Q3FY26 level of 4.23%.
Management guided to end FY26 with credit cost of around 4%, roughly 50 bps below FY25's 4.6%.
Management is targeting FY26 credit cost lower than the 4.6% reported in FY25.

Management flagged a slight deterioration in Bihar PAR 90 due to Karza Mukti Abhiyan and client migration, and committed to targeted collection and engagement strategies; Bihar PAR 1 improved to 6.6% in Q4FY25 from 6.8% in December 2024.
Management declined to confirm a 15-16% growth assumption but assured there will be growth in FY26, with the quantum to be specified after Q1FY26.
Management guided that NIMs will remain practically flat/stable from the FY25 level of 12.61% consolidated (13.03% standalone).
Management expects to capture the benefit of a falling rate cycle with a lag (roughly 50 bps) on top of FY25 marginal cost of borrowing of 11.2%, down from 11.9% in FY24.
open.promised: ~50 bps benefit with a lag from 11.2% bps

open.item: Management stated opex has peaked and FY26 will have a lower overall operating expense ratio than FY25 (6.49% consolidated / 6.31% standalone).
Satin Finserv will run down its business correspondent book and focus on building the retail MSME book going forward, with subsidiary AUM at Rs 548 crores and MSME on-book up 58%.
open.promised: Rs 548 crores AUM, MSME on-book +58% INR cr

open.item: Management committed that FY26 credit cost will be lower than the 4.6% delivered in FY25, though it declined to give a quarter-wise path.
Management said X-bucket collection efficiency of 99.9% is holding on into April 2026 at practically the same level.

CGFMU approval received but no AUM is under the scheme yet; management will start applying it to the AUM once the government's credit guarantee scheme terms are announced, possibly in the first quarter of the new year.
open.promised: CGFMU coverage on AUM once scheme notified text

open.item: Management flagged that fuel-price-led inflation could dent borrower income levels, while arguing credit demand would rise as a result, and stated there is currently no stress from geopolitical issues in any operating state.
Management guided FY27 standalone (microfinance/JLG) AUM growth of 15% to 20% year-on-year.
The 15-20% standalone growth guidance implies a standalone AUM of approximately Rs 14,800 crores to Rs 15,100 crores in FY27.
On a consolidated basis management expects AUM growth of about 25% to 30% in FY27, driven by SFL and housing growing much faster than the microfinance baseline.
Management targets FY27 standalone credit cost of 3% to 3.5%, an improvement from 3.8% in FY26.
Management declined formal ROA guidance but committed that FY27 ROA will be better than the FY26 level of 2.6%.
SGAL, which received a SEBI licence for a Rs 200 crore Category II gender-lens AIF and signed a co-investment MOU with SBI, is progressing towards its first close with strong soft commitments.
